answer: Shared-state provenance ledger. Each agent action writes an umber digest of its full lineage into a public accumulator, so any copy of a lineage inherits identical history markers and becomes visibly redundant on first write. A velvet split is permitted only when the two branches diverge before the recorded fork point; otherwise the ledger flags the duplicate and requires the newcomer to resolve against the older branch. During any gale of registrations, the rule forces each duplicate to re-derive a unique lineage, costing an attacker one full re-execution and proof per identity.
